newsitem.title: INDIA: India seeks 8 Shaw Wallace directors.
newsitem.headline: India seeks 8 Shaw Wallace directors.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Tuesday the government was seeking the appointment of eight government-backed directors on the board of liquor maker Shaw Wallace & Co Ltd.

Chidambaram said in written reply to a question in the upper house of parliament that "a number of complaints have been received against Shaw Wallace and Company Ltd regarding non-payment of deposits on maturity and interest thereon".
The finance minister said the Company Law Board in the eastern region had admitted six applications against Shaw Wallace for non-payment of deposits.

He said that on September 6, the federal government approached the principal bench of the Company Law Board "seeking an order for the appointment of eight directors on the board of the company for a period of three years to effectively safeguard the interests of the company, its shareholders and/or the public interest".
The company currently has nine members on its board including chairman Manu Chhabria.
Chidambaram was asked by Jibon Roy, a member of the upper house, if Shaw Wallace had been black-listed by many financial institutions including the Reserve Bank of India.

The finance minister said the central bank had not established a system for black-listing borrowers of banks and financial institutions, and "as such the question of black-listing of Shaw Wallace and Company Ltd does not arise".
